messages:
maria: Heads-up — we need to lock the 'safety-net' launch criteria for model-serving this cycle. Primary concerns: SLA banding, public docs, support/runbooks, monitoring signals, and pricing hooks. Who can own which piece and what are the immediate blockers?

ellen: I can own the SLA write-up. Need concrete latency and availability targets and the credit formula.

devin: From infra POV, latency targets determine autoscale policy and queueing. Any proposed numbers? 99.9/99.5/99.0? Also need sequence-length caveats.

maria: Proposal to start discussion: Enterprise 99.9, Dedicated 99.5, Standard 99.0. P99 latency targets (short seq): 250ms / 500ms / 1000ms. These are customer-facing SLAs — internal SLOs will be tighter.

raj: Those p99s look optimistic for long-context workloads. We should add an explicit clause: 'for requests <= 2k tokens' and a fallback policy for >2k tokens. Also recommend a documented degraded-mode behavior (graceful slowdown or model variant fallback).

samir: Support runway: we'll need playbooks for capacity incidents, QoS regressions, and billing disputes. I can draft the runbooks. Key items: triage steps, escalation matrix, sample customer comms, and rollback triggers.

lisa: Docs note: public SLA page + internal runbook links. For public page we must show how credits are calculated vs overage billing. Finance needs the precise formula. I'll loop them in.

ellen: Draft SLA table going into the doc. Quick snippet for clarity: 
```
Tier | Availability | P99 latency (<=2k tokens) | Monthly credit
Enterprise | 99.9% | 250ms | 10% monthly fee per 0.1% below
Dedicated | 99.5% | 500ms | 5% monthly fee per 0.25% below
Standard | 99.0% | 1000ms | service credit, case-by-case
```
Credit formula (internal): (downtime_minutes / total_minutes_in_month) * monthly_commit * credit_multiplier

devin: Infra telemetry to capture for SLA/ops: p50/p95/p99 latency, request rate, queue length, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and model-switch/failed-inference counters. Also add a canary toggle so we can roll policies per-customer.

maria: Good. Two other open things: pricing hooks (how to present burst usage and overage) and monitoring alerts thresholds + runbook links on the alert.

lisa: For pricing, propose 'committed capacity' + 'burst at x2 for y minutes' with billing breakpoint and automatic overage notifications. I'll sketch copy and example invoices for finance.

raj: On degraded-mode design: suggestion — automatic fallback to lower-capacity model variant + memo field explaining possible hallucination tradeoffs. Must be opt-out per-customer.

samir: Runbook checklist I'm planning: detection -> immediate mitigation (throttle/fallback) -> notify customers -> escalate to oncall -> postmortem owner. Will add sample templates.

ops-bot: incident created in #incidents/ops-1203 for missing runbook links (auto-detect).

maria: Action items summary: Ellen = SLA doc owner, produce public + internal versions; Samir = support & incident runbooks; Devin = autoscale + telemetry wiring + canary toggles; Lisa = pricing copy + billing formula; Raj = degraded-mode design + opt-out flow. Target: draft and owner review by EOW Thursday. If you can't hit that, flag now.

ellen: ack, I'll post a doc link by Tue. :eyes:

devin: Can do telemetry + canary plan, will need 2 sprints for rollout unless we pare back metrics.

samir: I'll aim for runbook draft Wed.

lisa: I'll sync with finance today and post the pricing hook draft tomorrow.

raj: I'll sketch degraded-mode and opt-out flow by Wed.

maria: Thanks — if anyone has edge cases (e.g., regulatory customers, on-prem/private) call them out. We'll compile into the public SLA footnotes. :shipit:
